text:
marta: quick design catch-up on the laned query surface. want to nail contracts between router, auth, and cache so we don't get surprises during cutover.
ashok: good call. two high-level goals: 1) no per-tenant policy duplication, 2) stable cache semantics so p95 doesn't regress.
rowan: my main worry is implicit assumptions in existing dashboards: many queries rely on eventual cache invalidation and sometimes rely on reads-after-write within <200ms. if the lane router changes where writes land we could break that.
syl: proposal: define a request contract header `X-Route-Intent: <intent>` where intent  {interactive, materialize, admin}. cache layer implements different invalidation strategies based on intent. e.g., interactive: strong prefix invalidation; materialize: best-effort TTL + async eviction hook.
marta: I like explicit intent. also suggest `X-Auth-Serial` header which is a short hash of auth decision so cache keys include auth context without expanding keyspace too much. keeps per-tenant isolation.
ashok: careful: embedding auth into cache keys increases cardinality. maybe `X-Auth-Serial` only when scope affects result (ex: tenant vs admin). default path omits it. need clear rules.
rowan: agree. add a lint check in the router config that marks routes where auth changes response shape; require `auth_serial=true` there.
syl: another catch: race during invalidation when a write goes to materialize lane and read hits interactive lane before tile refresh. solution: router emits an invalidation event to `console-invalidation` topic with `resource_id` + `lane_hint` and the cache subscribes. invalidation must be ordered-ish; we can include `seq` numbers from the writer to help.
marta: ordering is tricky across regions. we should design with monotonic per-resource seq but accept eventual ordering globally. interactive lane will always check a small write-log if the read is within 500ms of a write (lightweight check). that gives strong-read-after-write for a short window.
nashok: sounds like a hybrid: immediate invalidation (best-effort), plus short-lived read-check. cost? read-check adds an extra key lookup for recent-writes table but only for routes annotated `strong_r-a-w`.
rowan: let's be conservative and annotate only high-value dashboards initially. rollout can expand. also add metrics: `read-after-write-checks`, `read-after-write-hits`, and `invalidation-lag_ms`.
syl: RBAC: central PDP (policy decision point) issues capability tokens but router should still do a quick allow/deny to avoid routing obvious denies. lanes should re-verify capability signature and expiry. if a lane observes repeated signature failures from router, alert and fall back to deny-with-audit.
marta: key rotation note: lanes cache JWKs for 120s and accept `kid` rotation with a grace period of 90s. ops will coordinate rotations during low-traffic windows.
nashok: perf: router adds ~1ms median, ~6ms p95 in our microbench. acceptable for hosted but for private clouds we need a sidecar option where router logic runs in-process to get down to sub-ms.
rowan: sidecar adds deployment complexity. can we make router pluggable so private deployments can opt into either a remote router or local sidecar? config=`router.mode=remote|sidecar`.
syl: yes. also add health-check probes `/router/ready` and `/router/fast-path` so orchestrator can route locally when sidecar healthy.
marta: migration strategy: step 0: create route annotations and simulate routing decisions in shadow mode. step 1: enable routing for 1% of traffic with shadow=true. step 2: enable routing for small subset of tenants (canary) with full enforcement. step 3: expand and flip old surface off. each step gated on metrics and result-diff threshold.
nashok: diff harness: run 10k stored queries nightly comparing outputs from old surface vs laned surface. flag differences > 0.2% and bubble to owners. add small fuzzing to ignore harmless timing differences.
rowan: compatibility: for a short window we will allow `X-Legacy-Bypass` for specific service-accounts. that flag must be audited and expires automatically.
syl: operational telemetry: per-request tags: `lane`, `intent`, `auth_serial`, `invalidation_seq`, `raww_checked`. expose breakdown in console. create alerts: invalidation_lag_p95 > 500ms, raww_miss_rate > 5% for critical dashboards, router_p95 > 12ms.
marta: action items: 1) syl to sketch invalidation event schema + seq semantics (owner: syl). 2) ashok to write router config lint rules (owner: ashok). 3) rowan to scaffold diff harness and initial stored-queries (owner: rowan). 4) marta to draft migration playbook with canary gating (owner: marta). target doc deadline: 2024-08-09.
syl: will include sample event: `{ type: "invalidation", resource: "dash-123", seq: 12345, ts: 2024-07-22T15:30:00Z }` and note that lanes must tolerate out-of-order events up to N=3.
nashok: I'll add router linter rule examples, e.g. `route.auth_affects_response == true -> require auth_serial`.
rowan: I'll seed harness with top 200 dashboards, focusing on tenant-scoped queries first.
deploy-bot: note: infra-maintenance scheduled 2024-07-23 03:00 UTC may increase invalidation lag during window.
marta: thanks. one last ask: include billing tags in events so cost for materialize vs interactive can be attributed to customer. add `cost_tag` to metrics contract.
syl: noted. will include `cost_tag` and `est_cost_cents` in event/metric schema.
marta: ok closing thread, will spin up the RFC follow-up doc and tag owners. :rocket:
